papers.title_in_file: Improving Convergence for Quantum Variational Classifiers using Weight Re-Mapping
papers.what_it_is: Introduces weight re-mapping of variational circuit parameters and tests five functions on the Iris and Wine datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that weight re-mapping improved convergence in all tested settings with a variational classifier.
quotes: Our experiments show that weight re-mapping can improve convergence in all tested settings.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors report that weight re-mapping increased test accuracy on the Wine dataset by 10% over unmodified weights.
quotes: Additionally, we were able to demonstrate that weight re-mapping increased test accuracy for the Wine dataset by 10% over using unmodified weights.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.
assertions.reader_inference: The Iris gain is minor per the paper's own text, so the accuracy benefit is dataset dependent.

assertions.value: The authors evaluate a set of five re-mapping functions on the Iris and Wine datasets, using variational classifiers as an example.
quotes: We employ a set of five functions and evaluate them on the Iris and Wine datasets using variational classifiers as an example.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

papers.title_in_file: Towards Efficient Quantum Anomaly Detection: One-Class SVMs using Variable Subsampling and Randomized Measurements
papers.what_it_is: Tests randomized measurements and variable subsampling to cut the time cost of a quantum one-class SVM on synthetic and credit card fraud data.

assertions.value: The authors report that variable subsampling and randomized measurements reduced training time by up to 95% and inference time by up to 25%.
quotes: Experimental results demonstrate a substantial reduction in training and inference times by up to 95% and 25% respectively, employing these methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors report that improvements in average precision and F1 score over the classical kernel are discernible but minimally significant, diverging from a prior study they replicated, and state that the earlier result might rest on sample selection rather than a clear quantum advantage.
quotes: Our findings, diverging from (Kyriienko and Magnusson, 2022), reveal that while attainable improvements in average precision and F1 score over the classical kernel are discernible, they are minimally significant.
suggesting the original paper's results might hinge more on beneficial sample selection for the quantum IQP-like kernel rather than demonstrating a clear quantum advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors trained on random samples of 500 training and 125 test points from the Credit Card data, training the one-class SVM only on non-anomaly data, plus a synthetic dataset.
quotes: we employ random sampling to generate data sets comprising 500 training and 125 test data points, training the OC-SVM solely on non-anomaly data
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The small test set limits how far the precision comparison generalizes.

papers.title_in_file: Weight Re-Mapping for Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.what_it_is: Extends weight re-mapping to seven functions and eight classification datasets with angle and amplitude embedding.

assertions.value: The authors report that weight re-mapping consistently accelerated convergence regardless of the re-mapping function, and significantly raised accuracy in certain cases.
quotes: Our findings indicate that weight re-mapping not only consistently accelerates the convergence of VQCs, regardless of the specific re-mapping function employed, but also significantly increases accuracy in certain cases.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with angle embedding, averaged over all datasets, an improvement of at least 10% in convergence is always guaranteed.
quotes: In the case of Angle Embedding, which is usually the most common encoding, it can be seen how averaging on all the datasets at least an improvement of 10% in convergence is always guaranteed.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors report that the final-accuracy gain was significant with angle embedding but not so much with amplitude embedding, that the effect depends on the dataset, and that further studies are needed.
quotes: In our experiments this improvement in the final accuracy is significant when using the Angle Embedding as an encoding method, while not so much when using the Amplitude Embedding.
Further studies are needed to understand the dataset features and the techniques that could predict the relative performance of the different approaches.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors employ seven re-mapping functions on eight classification datasets, using variational classifiers as a representative example.
quotes: we employ seven distinct weight re-mapping functions to assess their impact on eight classification datasets, using variational classifiers as a representative example.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

papers.title_in_file: Parameterized Quantum Circuits as Feature Maps: Representation Quality and Readout Effects in Multispectral Land-Cover Classification
papers.what_it_is: Compares a local VQC readout with a fidelity-kernel SVM from the same trained circuit, and with classical baselines, on EuroSAT-MS land-cover classification.

assertions.value: The authors report that reusing the trained circuit as a fidelity kernel consistently improves over the standard local VQC readout.
quotes: Reusing the trained circuit as a fidelity kernel consistently improves over the standard local VQC readout, indicating that the learned quantum representation contains discriminative information not fully exploited by local measurements.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors report that classical RBF support-vector machines remained stronger overall, and ResNet-18 image models substantially outperformed all compact PCA-based approaches.
quotes: Classical RBF support-vector machines nevertheless remain stronger overall, while image-based ResNet-18 models substantially outperform all compact PCA-based approaches by exploiting spatial information discarded during preprocessing.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors evaluate all 45 one-versus-one class pairs of EuroSAT-MS with fixed splits, validation-based model selection and five optimization seeds.
quotes: Using EuroSAT-MS, we perform a controlled evaluation over all 45 one-versus-one class pairs with fixed trainvalidation-test splits, validation-based model selection, and five optimization seeds.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the results should not be interpreted as evidence of quantum advantage.
quotes: The results should not be interpreted as evidence of quantum advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope limit, Section I.

papers.what_it_is: Proposes a dissipative open-system quantum neuron with a tanh-like nonlinear activation, studied analytically and in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that their dissipative model exhibits differentiable, non-linear activation functions.
quotes: we show that this dissipative model based on repeated interactions, which allows for easy parametrization of input quantum information, exhibits differentiable, non-linear activation functions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical and simulated result in one paper; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum neuron responds as a hyperbolic tangent-like activation that can be controlled by the value of J.
quotes: We show that the quantum neuron responds as a hyperbolic tangent-like activation which can be controlled by the value of J.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical and simulated result in one paper; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulations use the QuTiP package in Python; the paper reports no hardware run.
quotes: The simulations are carried out by using QUTIP package in Python
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: No quantum hardware experiment appears in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the current state of the art already allows experimental implementation of small-scale models of the proposed network.
quotes: Furthermore, the current state-of-the-art already allows for the experimental implementation of small-scale models of the proposed quantum neural network.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors assert this without an experiment in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Investigating Quantum Many-Body Systems with Tensor Networks, Machine Learning and Quantum Computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Chapter 1 motivation, end of Chapter 4 (variational algorithms), Chapter 8 (introduction, proposal, results, outlook). Chapters 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 skimmed by conclusion only.
papers.what_it_is: PhD thesis on tensor-network phase mapping with anomaly detection, extended to variational quantum anomaly detection run on an IBM device.

assertions.value: The authors state that simulation and quantum machine learning routines are performed on the same device, demonstrated in classical simulation and on a physical IBM quantum computer.
quotes: Both simulation and QML routines are performed on the same device, which we demonstrate both in classical simulation and on a physical quantum computer hosted by IBM.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors state that the main bottleneck of variational quantum anomaly detection is noise in real devices.
quotes: Currently, the main bottleneck of VQAD is the presence of noise in real devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis states its own limit, Section 8.4.

assertions.value: The authors ran the device experiment on 5 qubits of ibmq_jakarta, with pre-optimized parameters from a noisy simulation as initial guesses.
quotes: For this task, we use the L = 5 qubits on ibmq_jakarta
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis states its own setup, Section 8.3.

assertions.value: The author states that variational algorithms are likely not scalable beyond what tensor network methods reach and serve more as a proof of principle.
quotes: variational algorithms are likely not scalable to system sizes that are beyond what is reachable with tensor network methods and serve more as a proof of principle
assertions.certainty_reason: An author judgment citing other work, not a result of the thesis.

papers.title_in_file: Encoding Numerical Data for Generative Quantum Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: Shows that the binary code used to encode numeric data matters for quantum circuit Born machines, and that a reflected Gray code often trains better.

assertions.value: The authors report that QCBMs using the reflected Gray code learn faster and more accurately than those with the standard binary code in most cases, outperforming it in 80% of their numerical simulations.
quotes: we verify that, in most cases, QCBMs using the reflected Gray code learn faster and more accurately than those with standard binary code.
which outperforms the standard code in 80% of our numerical simulations
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors state that the standard encoding requires models to learn correlations that are solely an artifact of how the data is encoded.
quotes: show that it requires the models to learn correlations that are solely an artifact of the way the data is encoded
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical argument plus simulation; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors state that different data structures might require different inductive biases and different binary encodings; the tests used datasets drawn from low-dimensional probability distributions.
quotes: We stress, however, that different structures in the data might require different inductive biases and therefore different binary encodings.
Considering datasets drawn from various low-dimensional probability distributions
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope, Section IV.

papers.title_in_file: Variational quantum-neural hybrid imaginary time evolution
papers.what_it_is: Proposes VQNHITE, a neural-network-assisted variational imaginary time evolution, tested by simulation on Heisenberg spin chains.

assertions.value: The authors report that VQNHITE consistently achieves higher fidelity with the exact ITE state than VITE.
quotes: The results demonstrate that VQNHITE consistently achieves higher fidelity with the exact ITE state compared to VITE.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study; the coordinator grades.

assertions.value: The authors tested the method by numerical simulation on Heisenberg spin chains with nearest-neighbor and all-to-all circuit connectivities.
quotes: We tested our approach with numerical simulations on Heisenberg spin chains under both nearest-neighbor and all-to-all circuit connectivities.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that extending the method to larger-scale systems is future work, and that the initialization step raises computational time and sampling costs compared to VITE.
quotes: Future work includes extending VQNHITE to largerscale systems and exploring alternative neural-network architectures
Although this procedure increases the computational time and sampling costs compared to the VITE
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and cost, Section VI.
